title: Quick Prostate Cancer Test
summary: Ten personal questions about prostate changes and risk context, followed by a cautious next-step profile.

landing.intro: Have you noticed changes that are easy to dismiss as ageing? Answer 10 quick questions about the symptoms and risk factors that may matter.

about.body:
This ten-question personal check asks about urinary changes, blood, discomfort, persistent pain and relevant risk context. It groups your answers into a cautious next-step profile; it does not calculate your likelihood of cancer.

Prostate cancer may cause no symptoms at first, and urinary changes often have non-cancerous causes such as benign prostate enlargement, infection or inflammation. New, persistent or worsening changes should still be discussed with a qualified healthcare professional.

howToPlay.title: How to Play
steps: Choose the answer that most closely matches your recent experience.
Think about changes that are new, persistent or getting worse.
Reveal your next-step profile after all ten questions.

about.disclaimer: For general information only. This is not a diagnostic test, validated symptom checker, risk calculator, PSA test or medical screening tool. It cannot confirm or rule out prostate cancer or any other condition. Seek urgent medical care for inability to urinate, severe or rapidly worsening pain, heavy bleeding, large blood clots or feeling seriously unwell.

stage-1.preAdCopy: Your ten answers have been reviewed and your cautious next-step profile is ready to reveal.

profile-1.title: No Recent Pattern Stood Out
profile-1.copy: Your answers did not highlight a current symptom pattern. That cannot rule out prostate cancer, which may cause no early symptoms. Personal risk, age and screening decisions still need an individual discussion with a healthcare professional.

profile-2.title: A Prostate Check Is Worth Considering
profile-2.copy: Your answers centred on urine flow, starting, frequency or urgency. These changes often have non-cancerous explanations, but new, persistent or worsening symptoms should be discussed with a qualified healthcare professional.

profile-3.tier: PAIN OR BLEEDING RESPONSES STOOD OUT
profile-3.title: Do Not Keep Guessing At The Cause
profile-3.copy: Your answers included discomfort, persistent pain or possible blood. Arrange timely medical advice. Seek urgent care for inability to urinate, severe or rapidly worsening pain, heavy bleeding, large clots or feeling seriously unwell.

profile-4.tier: RISK OR NEXT-STEP CONTEXT STOOD OUT
profile-4.title: Put Your Full Picture In Context
profile-4.copy: Your answers highlighted personal risk context, persistent changes or action you may already be considering. A healthcare professional can review age, ancestry, family history and symptoms together and discuss whether examination or testing is appropriate.
